input.content: Pattern: version-skew backward-compat break from hard-asserting a new response field. A client increment that starts requiring a new success-receipt field (e.g. `if response.get("applied") is not True: raise`) breaks every call against an already-released provider that does not yet emit that field — the getter returns None and the strict `is not True` check fails. Symptom: ordinary operations throw against the supported baseline even though the provider actually applied the change (false-negative; data persisted but caller sees failure). Root cause: treating absence of the new field as rejection instead of as a legacy provider that does not participate. Fix: only reject on an explicit negative (`if response.get("applied") is False: raise`) so a missing field = backward-compatible success; or gate the receipt requirement behind a negotiated capability/flag. Always review a new consumer's added request/response fields against the oldest supported provider the delivery contract names (git tag), not against an updated test mock.
